text:
Tom: Hey team, customer (acme-inc) reporting a sudden p95/p99 latency spike after they switched to the new model variant `redwood-llama-long-v2`. Symptoms: completion requests for >20k token contexts take 3-5x longer, some timeouts at p99. Repro steps attached below.

Marie: thanks Tom — can you paste the smallest repro you have and the exact API call they used? also which region and whether Dedicated/Hosted?

Tom: Hosted (us-west-2). Example curl they used:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-llama-long-v2","input":"<20k token doc + question>","max_output_tokens":512,"stream":false}'
```

Tom: They say switching back to `redwood-llama-long-v1` restores p99 to normal. Also noticed a regen with identical prompt sometimes faster — looks non-deterministic.

ops-bot: ALERT: latency.p99 spike for `redwood-llama-long-v2` in us-west-2 detected at 2026-02-28T14:12:07Z — +310% vs baseline. Incident ID: INC-20260228-42 :rotating_light:

Alex: I'm looking at runtime traces now. Initial observation: large increase in KV cache misses per request for the v2 variant. KV cache hit rate dropped from ~87% to ~42 on long-context traffic. That would amplify tokens generated and trigger more kernel launches.

Sasha: interesting — the model update included a tokenizer normalization tweak (normalization of U+2028, preserving control markers) that we shipped to reduce off-by-one in RLHF prompts. Could that change token alignment and blow up context token counts?

Alex: yes, changed tokenization can change segmentation boundaries which cascades into different cache keys and prefix lengths. If the same logical prompt tokenizes differently, cached KV entries won't match.

Marie: Tom, can you ask customer for raw byte length and token counts under both model versions? Also check whether they used `preserve_whitespace` or custom pre-token transforms.

Tom: Sent their logs. They attached counts: original text ~18000 chars -> v1 tokenized = 11,300 tokens; v2 tokenized = 13,900 tokens. So +23% token inflation. That maps pretty well to the observed extra compute.

Alex: That token inflation alone explains a lot of p95 pressure, but p99 is still higher than expected. I'm seeing spikes where KV miss + repeated attention recompute caused tail latency hits (long running GPU scheduler ops).

Sasha: quick theory: v2 introduces an extra sentinel token around paragraph breaks which increases effective sequence length and causes certain batched requests to exceed optimized kernel path (we only use the fast fused kernel up to 16k tokens). When it falls back to slow kernel, latency multiplies.

Alex: confirmed in profiler: requests crossing the 16k token threshold go from ~150ms/token to ~520ms/token on our current kernel. That threshold line up with their token inflation.

Marie: ok concrete mitigations: 1) Temporary revert model variant for hosted customers (roll back to v1) 2) Enable server-side token normalization shim that applies v1-compatible tokenization for the affected route 3) Add automatic re-routing rule: requests with predicted tokenized length >14k get routed to dedicated nodes with the slow kernel optimized for longer contexts (if customer has Dedicated) 4) Short-term: set a soft reject/warning if predicted tokens > 14k with suggestion to chunk. Thoughts?

Alex: I can prepare a hotfix route to apply a tokenization compatibility layer at the edge — rewrites that normalize U+2028 -> space and remove sentinels. That should restore most KV hits. I'll prepare a canary patch and run a canary on 5% of traffic.

Sasha: long-term we need: (a) a tokenizer delta test in the model onboarding pipeline: run synthetic long-context corpora, measure token inflation and kernel-path crossing, (b) upgrade/extend fused kernels to handle the new threshold or add a fallback pre-compile for long sequences. I'll open infra tickets.

Tom: Customer is ok with a temporary revert while we investigate. They need a timeline — can we do the rollback now?

Alex: I can orchestrate a rollback of `redwood-llama-long-v2` traffic to v1 for hosted in us-west-2. Plan: set traffic split to 0% v2 -> 100% v1, run for 30m, monitor p95/p99, then rollback globally if stable. I'll run the change at :30 UTC.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Starting rollout job RB-20260228-77: route-change `redwood-llama-long-v2` -> 0% (canary 0%) in us-west-2 by Alex.

Alex: rollout done. Metrics: within 10 minutes, p99 dropped ~60% and p95 back near baseline for the customer's route. KV hit rates recovered to ~84%. Will keep watching for 1 hour.

Marie: please file a customer-facing postmortem and include the token delta numbers, the workaround (rollback + token shim), and recommended steps for customers with long contexts. Also check billing implications — token inflation might increase costs.

Sasha: created infra ticket INF-20260228-19 "Tokenizer delta testing + kernel threshold" with priority P1. Also adding unit in model onboarding: run 1000 long-doc samples and measure token delta and kernel path crossing.

Tom: Customer updated: thanks for quick fix, waiting on postmortem. They asked: can you add a flag on API to force v1 tokenization per-request?

Alex: we can add `tokenizer_compat: "v1"` as a short-term API parameter behind feature flag. Ops: will gate to internal and to customers in escalation path first.

Marie: assign follow-ups: Alex -> edge token shim & per-request flag (ETA 24h), Sasha -> infra ticket + onboarding tests (ETA 72h), Product -> communicate model change process to customers and add token-delta check (ETA 5 days). I'll draft the postmortem now.

ops-bot: NOTE: incident INC-20260228-42 resolved (monitoring indicates return to baseline after rollback).

Alex: added quick repro script for engineering to validate locally:

```
# repro-run (internal)
repro-run --model redwood-llama-long-v2 --input samples/long_docs/001.txt --count_tokens --profile
```
Sasha: small follow-up: we should also include a change log on the model catalog page highlighting tokenizer behavior changes (breaking for long context). People expect binary compatibility.

Marie: nice work team. Closing channel once postmortem draft + customer note are out. :white_check_mark:

Tom: will paste customer note link here when it's sent. Thanks all!
